attachments.description: The word agriculture is a late Middle English adaptation of Latin agricultura, from ager, “field”, and cultura, “cultivation” or “growing”. Agriculture usually refers to human activities consisting in the cultivation of plants, fungi, and other life forms for obtaining products used to sustain and enhance human life.

attachments.name: Could underwater farming feed the world?
attachments.description: Worldwide, farmland consumes an area roughly the size of Canada and the United States put together. It takes that much land to produce enough fruits, vegetables, and grains to feed the world, to say nothing of the millions of acres given over to cows, sheep and other livestock for grazing.

attachments.name: Can Underwater Farms Help Fight Climate Change?

attachments.name: Mariculture: Farming the Ocean to Feed a Future Population of 10 Billion Humans
attachments.description: Aquaculture is the marine equivalent of agriculture. Farming aquatic flora and fauna for human consumption. Mariculture is the same thing but carried out offshore in the open ocean rather than the artificial pools on land where aquaculture is most commonly performed.
